legend: Accidentally_Coder, a renowned coder from CSEland, is in a dilemma – she wants to give her friend, The_Author, a special gift. After thinking for a while, she went to her favorite shop at Zindabazar and bought an empty matrix A%%ZSMJ0%% of size n×n%%ZSMJ1%%. She knows that her friend loves numbers which are power of 2%%ZSMJ2%%. So she decided to fill the matrix in a way that the following conditions hold:
For each 1≤i≤n%%ZSMJ3%%, 1≤j≤n%%ZSMJ4%%, Ai,j%%ZSMJ5%% is an integer and 1≤Ai,j≤109%%ZSMJ6%% holds
The sum of numbers in each row is a power of 2%%ZSMJ7%% (that is, ∑nj=1Ai,j%%ZSMJ8%% should be a power of 2%%ZSMJ9%% for each 1≤i≤n%%ZSMJ10%%)
The sum of numbers in each column is a power of 2%%ZSMJ11%% (that is, ∑ni=1Ai,j%%ZSMJ12%% should be a power of 2%%ZSMJ13%% for each 1≤j≤n%%ZSMJ14%%)

The sum of numbers in each of the primary and secondary diagonals is a power of 2%%ZSMJ15%% (that is, ∑ni=1Ai,i%%ZSMJ16%% should be a power of 2%%ZSMJ17%% and ∑ni=1Ai,n+1−i%%ZSMJ18%% should be a power of 2%%ZSMJ19%%)
A number P%%ZSMJ20%% is considered a power of 2%%ZSMJ21%%, if there is some integer i%%ZSMJ22%%(0≤i)%%ZSMJ23%%, for which P=2i%%ZSMJ24%%
Your task is to find any matrix of size n×n%%ZSMJ25%% satisfying these conditions or report that no such matrix exists.
input: The only line in the input contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ26%% (1≤n≤1000)%%ZSMJ27%%.
output: If a solution exists, output n%%ZSMJ28%% lines, each containing n%%ZSMJ29%% integers in range [1,109]%%ZSMJ30%%, the numbers of the matrix. Otherwise, output −1%%ZSMJ31%% on a single line.
